item.title: Plane crashed after 3D-printed part collapsed
item.description:
📝 Plane crashed after 3D-printed part collapsed4 hours agoShareSaveMaisie LillywhiteGloucestershireShareSaveAir Accidents Investigation BranchThe sole crew member sustained minor injuries in the crash, which destroyed the light aircraftA plane crashed after a 3D-printed part softened and collapsed, causing its engine to lose power, a report has found. The aircraft crashed into a landing aid system at Gloucestershire Airport in Staverton on 18 March at 13:04 GMT, after its engine lost power. More on this storyRunway closed after aircraft makes 'emergency landing'Related internet linksAir Accident Investigation BranchStavertonGloucestershire AirportGloucestershire.
🔗 Read more: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1w932vqye0o

item.title: CJEU has made it effectively impossible to run a user-generated platform legally
item.description:
📝 That advertisement contained photographs of that applicant, which had been used without her consent, along with her telephone number. When contacted by the applicant in the main proceedings, Russmedia Digital removed the advertisement from its website less than one hour after receiving that request. In that regard, it held that Russmedia could not be criticised for failing to take measures to prevent the online distribution of the defamatory advertisement at issue in the main proceedings, given that it had rapidly removed that advertisement at the request of the applicant in the main proceedings.
